text.p: Petrolite Corp, which earlier reported a rise in fiscal first quarter profits, said it expects further year-over-year earnings gains as fiscal 1997 progresses.
Earlier, it reported earnings for the first quarter ended January 31 of $0.73, excluding gains, up from $0.29 a year ago. Net earnings after gains for the quarter were $1.28 a share.
"This record-setting performance in the first quarter marked the fifth consecutive quarter of earnings growth," Paul Hatfield, chairman, said in a statement.
He added that the turnaround from declines in prior years resulted from a strategic plan to increase shareholder value, which was implemented at the start of fiscal 1996.
"These results exceeded our plan, which we believe will generate futher year-over-year earnings as 1997 progresses," Hatfield said.
Petrolite earned $1.68 a share in fiscal 1996.
Gains for the first quarter included $700,000 or $0.06 a share from the extension of an option to amend its business alliance with Energy BioSystems Corp of Houston.
In exchange for granting the option, Petrolite received $1.0 million and will continue to provide support to an Energy BioSystems pilot plant through December 31, 1998.
Petrolite is a specialty chemical company.
